_note: Pre-checked diagnosis for public/media/demo-chair.mp4. Uploading this exact sample clip returns this diagnosis; other uploads are diagnosed live by Claude.
summary: The chair rocks when pushed because the front-left leg has worked loose where it meets the seat rail. The old glue has failed, the screw holding the joint has backed out of a stripped hole, and one corner bracket underneath is missing a screw. Re-glue, re-seat the screw and it will be as solid as new.

markers.label: Front-left leg shifts at the joint
markers.detail: The whole chair rocks from this one corner when pushed.

markers.label: Screw backing out of the joint
markers.detail: The joint has opened up and the screw is no longer biting: its hole is stripped.

markers.label: Old glue has failed
markers.detail: Dried glue is flaking out of the joint, so it no longer holds.

markers.label: Bracket missing a screw
markers.detail: The front-left corner bracket has an empty screw hole.

steps.title: Flip the chair and remove the bracket
steps.detail: Lay the chair upside down on a towel and unscrew the front-left corner bracket.

steps.title: Pull out the loose screw
steps.detail: Back the screw out of the joint completely and scrape the old flaking glue off both surfaces.

steps.title: Fix the stripped hole
steps.detail: Dip two hardwood dowel slivers in glue, tap them into the screw hole and snap them off flush.

steps.title: Re-glue the joint
steps.detail: Spread wood glue on the joint, press the leg back into place and drive a new #8 screw in snugly.

steps.title: Refit the bracket
steps.detail: Put the bracket back with two new screws, including the one that was missing.

steps.title: Let it set and test
steps.detail: Wait an hour for the glue to grab, then push the chair like in your video. It shouldn't move.

parts.name: #8 wood screws, 1¼ in
parts.why: Replaces the backed-out and missing screws

parts.name: Hardwood dowel slivers
parts.query: hardwood dowel pins for stripped screw holes

safety: Let the glue set for an hour before sitting on the chair.

fixed.label: Repaired chair
fixed.reason: The chair stays still when pushed, the joint is closed with no gap, the screw sits flush and the bracket has both screws. All four faults from the original video are resolved.

leaking.label: Still wobbly
leaking.sub: See what happens if it isn't fixed
leaking.reason: The front-left leg still shifts at 0:02 and the joint gap is still open at 0:05. The repair is not complete.
